ev.q: In September 2023, a 10th U.S. case of locally acquired malaria was diagnosed, in Arkansas.
Seven of eight local hospitals reported ability to examine and interpret thick and thin blood smears, and two reported use of malaria RDTs.
Of the 244 total mosquitos collected, 25 female Anopheles mosquitoes were identified and sent to CDC for Plasmodium testing**; all specimens tested negative.
Eight potential malaria cases were identified; all patients received alternative diagnoses.
Of the 244 total mosquitos collected, 25 female Anopheles mosquitoes were identified

public_health_question.v: How was a locally acquired mosquito-transmitted P. vivax malaria case in Arkansas investigated and responded to, and was there evidence of further local transmission?

ev.q: The public health response included case investigation and surveillance, mosquito surveillance and control, assessment of hospital preparedness, and clinical and public outreach.
Locally Acquired (Autochthonous) Mosquito-Transmitted Plasmodium vivax Malaria — Saline County, Arkansas, September 2023
A case of locally acquired (autochthonous) mosquito-transmitted Plasmodium vivax malaria was diagnosed in Arkansas in September 2023.
ADH confirmed the patient had never traveled internationally and did not have other risk factors for acquiring malaria in the United States.
prospective enhanced case finding was implemented using the Electronic Surveillance System for the Early Notification of Community-Based Epidemics (ESSENCE) syndromic surveillance system.
ADH began enhanced mosquito surveillance at two sites in Saline County near the patient’s residence
